title: Repo garbage collector: quarantine unused files to a timestamped reversible folder (T1 core)
desc: Core skill for the repo GC: find UNUSED/UNREFERENCED files+scripts and MOVE (never delete) them to .tmp/unused-<timestamp>/<relpath>/ -- reversible quarantine. Keeps the repo root + tools/ clean of -proto/-demix/-bak orphans. Conservative, dry-run-first, ROOT-reviewed.
steps: CORE CONCEPT (user 2026-06-18): a repo GC finds UNUSED / UNREFERENCED files and SCRIPTS and QUARANTINES them -- MOVES (never deletes) each to .tmp/unused-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>/<original-relative-path>/, a TIMESTAMPED folder per run so each sweep is distinguishable, restorable as a whole, and reversible (restore = move back). WHY: the repo root + tools/ accumulate -proto / -proto-proto / -demix / -bak* / -probe / -prove / -test / -debug / -partial / -minimal / -old orphans that make every future read token-hostile.

UNUSED DETECTION (conservative -- ALL must hold to quarantine): (a) the file's BASENAME is NOT referenced (grep) anywhere in the repo's tracked source / .md / settings; (b) it matches a throwaway SUFFIX (the list above + .tmp) OR is not git-tracked-and-recently-modified; (c) it is NOT an ENTRY POINT -- wkharness*.ps1 family mains, anything referenced in ~/.claude/settings.json or a family settings.json, the canonical Verify-* / *-classifier / guards / wkharness-* files. FAIL-SAFE: when UNSURE whether a file is referenced, KEEP it -- a false-quarantine of an active file is the only real danger, and it is reversible but noisy.
SAFETY + WORKFLOW: DRY-RUN by DEFAULT -- print a table (file

would-move-to) + a summary count; a -Apply switch performs the moves only after ROOT reviews the dry-run. NEVER quarantine: a referenced/git-active file, an entry point, CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / AGENTS.md / README, or anything under .git. Timestamped folder makes 'oops, restore that whole run' a one-liner.

INTEGRATION: a standalone tool (prototype tools/wkgc-proto.ps1, Sonnet-built) does the quarantine; wkdoctor surfaces the unused-file COUNT as a 'repo cleanliness' health check so messiness is visible in the routine checkup. Verify it with the synthetic/live/static method (synthetic temp dir with a referenced file + an entry-point-named file + a -proto orphan -> asserts it keeps the first two, flags only the orphan).

REVERSIBILITY IS THE WHOLE POINT: because nothing is deleted and the path structure is preserved under unused-<ts>/, a wrong call costs nothing -- move it back. This is why a CONSERVATIVE-but-active GC beats both 'never clean' (token-hostile repo) and 'delete unused' (irreversible, scary).
